First, we apply the sum rule and write our repeated integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x
$$

Since the domain of integration $R=[0,4]\times [1,2]\times [0,1]$ is a rectangular box, and each integrand can be expressed as $f(x)\cdot g(y)\cdot h(z),$ we can rewrite our sum of repeated integrals as follows:

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z-{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z
$$

Let's evaluate each of these separately:

- For the first product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}{z}^{3}\,\text{d}z & ={[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{0}^{4}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{1}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{z}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(8-0)(\frac{8}{3}-\frac{1}{3})(\frac{1}{4}-0) \\  & =8(\frac{7}{3})(\frac{1}{4}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}\text{d}x{\int }_{1}^{2}\text{d}y\,{\int }_{0}^{1}z\,\text{d}z & =(4-0)\cdot (2-1)\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{z}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4\cdot 1\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x{y}^{2}{z}^{3}-z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x=\frac{14}{3}-2=\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
